This city is located in the Desert of Paran, where Allah created the Zamzam Well for Hajar and Ismail. The Black Stone is set in silver in this city's Kaaba [kah-ah-bah], around which pilgrims walk during the Hajj, and toward which Muslims face when praying. Name this Islamic holy city, the birthplace of Muhammad.

A pressure associated with this process is a colligative property proportional to mass and temperature, and is defined as the hydrostatic pressure necessary to counteract this process. A "reverse" form of this process is sometimes used to purify water. Name this movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration.

The size of these objects is given by the Schwarzschild radius. According to quantum mechanics, these objects emit Hawking radiation. One of them, Sagittarius A Star, sits at the center of our galaxy and has four million times the mass of our sun. What are these objects in outer space from which supposedly nothing, not even light, can escape?

The "law of" these objects states that the torque on one side is equal to the torque on the other side. These objects can be classified as first class, second class, or third class depending on the location of the fulcrum. Name these simple machines, familiar examples of which include a wheelbarrow and see-saw.

The DNA in this organelle is inherited only from the mother. The inner membrane of this organelle contains folds known as cristae and encloses its matrix. This organelle is the site of oxidative phosphorylation, which occurs at the end of the electron transport chain. Name this organelle responsible for cellular respiration, which produces ATP and thus provides energy for the cell.

The Euler line passes through the orthocenter, circumcenter, and centroid in this figure. The area of this polygon can be found by halving the product of two sides and the sine of the angle opposite of the third side or by simply using Heron's formula. It is the only polygon that cannot be concave, because its angles must add to 180 degrees. Name this polygon with three sides.

One theory of this entity's creation states that a Mars-sized body named Theia collided with its parent planet. This object exhibits synchronous rotation with its parent planet, and that rotation results in the namesake "dark side" of this object. The Sea of Tranquility lies on, what astronomical body responsible for the Earth's tides, its largest natural satellite?

The Andean type of these entities occurs beneath a continental plate, and it is at these sites that about 20% of Earth's crust has been consumed. This antithesis of the mid-oceanic ridge is usually typified by lines of volcanoes running parallel near an oceanic trench. Identify this region where tectonic plates collide, and one goes underneath the other.

One piece of evidence that supports its existence is that the Caledonian mountains of Northern Europe are a continuation of the Appalachian Mountains. This entity broke up into Laurasia and Gondwanaland. Alfred Wegener coined its name during a lecture in which he discussed his theory of continental drift. Identify this supercontinent theorized to have existed 250 million years ago.

Two liquids are said to be immiscible if they cannot combine to form this type of mixture. In the most common form of this mixture, solid particles are small enough to completely dissolve in a liquid. Name this type of mixture that is not a colloid or suspension, an example of which is sugar dissolved in water.

This constellation is often interpreted as fighting Taurus with his dogs Canis Minor and Canis Major. Stars within this constellation include the "amazon star" Bellatrix, the red giant Betelgeuse, and Rigel. It is most easily recognizable by the three stars making up the belt of the figure in this constellation. Name this constellation also known as "the Hunter."

The harmonic one of n numbers in a data set is n divided by the sum of the reciprocals of the numbers. The geometric one is the nth root of the product of the numbers. The geometric one is always less than or equal to the arithmetic one. What is this term in mathematics—the arithmetic one being the sum of the numbers divided by n?

One part of this process sees the formation of the 5-carbon sugar ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate. In the light dependent reactions in this process, NADPH and ATP are produced by using energy harvested from light by chlorophyll. This process can be carried out by cyanobacteria and algae, though it is most associated with plants. Name this process which converts carbon dioxide to sugars such as glucose.

Alternatives to it include the Knoop test, the Vickers test, and measurement with a sclerometer. Although decimal values are allowed, it is more common to say that an object's value is between that of two reference materials based on the scratch test. Corundum has a value of nine and talc has a value of one on, what scale that measures a mineral's hardness?

Bernoulli is credited with the discovery of this constant when he attempted to find the value of the limit as n approaches infinity of the quantity one plus one over n to the nth power. This constant is used when finding interest compounded continuously and when modeling exponential growth, and it is the base of the natural logarithm. Name this constant, approximately equal to 2.71828.

This macromolecule can be artificially copied using the polymerase chain reaction. Okazaki fragments can form on its lagging strand during its replication. Chargaff proposed rules governing the pairing of this macromolecule's bases, adenine, thymine, guanine, and cytosine. Watson and Crick discovered its double helix shape. Name this nucleic acid, the human genetic material.

When air resistance exactly counteracts this force, an object has reached terminal velocity. The escape velocity is the minimum speed needed to overcome the effects of this force. On Earth, this force acts to accelerate a body at nine point eight meters per second squared. Name this force responsible for keeping objects on the ground.

The density of objects drops to almost zero at this region's namesake cliff. Most of the objects found here are called cubewanos. The Oort cloud ends at the beginning of this region's elliptic. Identify this area at the edge of the solar system that houses thousands of short period comets, Eris, and Pluto.

One form of this concept is equal to the product of charge and voltage. For a spring, this quantity is given by one-half times the spring constant times the square of the distance from equilibrium. The gravitational form of this quantity is equal to an object's weight times its height. Give this "stored" energy that is converted into kinetic energy.

The Dewar equation defines this quantity for density-dependent variables. Species that exhibit exponential population growth appear to lack this value, and in logistic population growth, the per capita rate of increase approaches zero near this value. Name this ecological term, often denoted k, which is the maximum population that can be sustained by an ecosystem.

Two of these entities are responsible for the Great Rift Valley located in East Africa. Subduction zones are found along them. Several of them are responsible for the area of volcanic activity known as the Ring of Fire, though movement along them more famously causes earthquakes. Identify these gaps in the Earth's crust, which include one in California called the San Andreas.

This term denotes any algebraic expression written as the quotient of two polynomials. If the discriminant of a quadratic equation is a perfect square, then both roots of that equation are of this type. All numbers denoted by this term are algebraic. Give this term that denotes any number that can be written as a over b, where a and b are integers.

The heat of fusion is the amount of heat that must be added to a substance for this process to occur without a change in temperature. Salt is placed on roads to favor this process over its opposite. At atmospheric pressure, ice undergoes this process at zero degrees Celsius. Name this conversion from solids into liquids, whose opposite is freezing.

This author's book The Descent of Man was inspired by his encounter with natives of Tierra del Fuego when he voyaged with Robert Fitzroy on HMS Beagle. A group of finches with differing beaks were collected in the Galapagos by, what British scientist who proposed the theory of evolution in The Origin of Species?

Amazonstone and cleavelandite are members of this group of minerals. Samples of it which show a high opalescence are traded as moonstone, and some with a yellow or orange tint are sold as sunstone. The plagioclase and alkali forms of this mineral are prevalent in granite. Made of aluminum, silicon, and either calcium, sodium, or potassium, name this mineral, number 6 on the Mohs scale of hardness.

By mass, most of the atmosphere is contained within this layer, as it is the densest. Reaching a maximum height of about 16 kilometers at the equator, the boundary immediately above it is the coldest part of the atmosphere, and the jet stream is strongest just below that pause. Most weather systems are contained within this layer. Name this lowest layer of the atmosphere.

The fundamental theorem of arithmetic states that every positive integer can be uniquely represented as a product of these numbers. Special types of these numbers are named after Fermat and Mersenne. To find these numbers, one may use the Sieve of Eratosthenes (air-uh-TOSS- then-eez"), in which one crosses off all multiples of two, then all multiples of three, and so on. Give these numbers whose only factors are one and themselves.

This compound is converted to Vitamin D in the presence of ultraviolet-B light. It is carried in the blood by lipoproteins, with the "good" kind carried by high-density ones. The "bad" kind, carried by LDLs, can build up on arteries to form plaques. 300 milligrams per day is the recommended dietary allowance of what waxy substance, high levels of which place an individual at greater risk for heart disease?

Two stars in this asterism, Mizar and Alcor, have been called the Horse and Rider. Though the North Star is not in this asterism, one can find it by tracing a line from Merak and Dubhe, which make up one side of this asterism's title feature. Name this group of about seven stars found in Ursa Major, which also comes in a "little" version.

One part of these structures is covered with cementum. They are divided into a "crown" and a "root," and are covered with enamel. "Wisdom" ones are often removed by an oral surgeon. They can be divided into incisors, canines, premolars, and molars. Name these structures used to chew food.

In publishing, this six-letter term describes a set of journal issues published in the same year. It also describes the sound level output from a computer or television. Density equals mass divided by a quantity with this name. Give this term for the amount of space an object occupies, which for a cube equals side length cubed.

This element's allotropes include nanotubes and fullerenes. Another allotrope of this element consists of thin hexagonal sheets and is known as graphite. This element is bound to four hydrogen atoms in methane. Name this element that makes up diamonds, which has atomic number six and symbol C.

For any odd number greater than one, there exists one of these types of sets where that number is the smallest of the three elements. By definition, all numbers in these kinds of sets are integers. Common example of this type of set are (8, 15, 17); (5, 12, 13); and (3, 4, 5). Name these sets of three integers a, b, and c which satisfy the equation a squared plus b squared equals c squared.

"Wedge" and "rope" are informal terms used to denote large and small forms of these phenomena. Twenty-eight different damage indicators help measure their severity via the enhanced Fujita scale. These phenomena occur when a funnel cloud touches the ground. Name these violently rotating windstorms that most often occur in their namesake "Alley" in the American Midwest.

Venus' hairstone consists of this mineral with rutile interspersed within. Citrine is formed through heating the "smoky" form of this mineral, whose rarer forms consist of a "rose" form as well as amethyst. Sandstone is primarily composed of this mineral. Silicon dioxide is the primary composition of, what mineral, number 8 on the Mohs scale, which is used in glass and sandpaper?

PH in this fluid is regulated by the bicarbonate ion buffer system. Cells in this fluid include leukocytes and erythrocytes, while platelets help form clots that stop its flow. It is carried in arteries and veins. Name this fluid that delivers oxygen and nutrients to cells and is pumped by the heart.

This is the only number that satisfies the equation sine x equals x. The additive inverse property says that the sum of any number and its additive inverse equals this number, while the additive identity property says that any number plus this number equals the original number. Name this only non-positive whole number, which yields itself when multiplied by any number.

Cherenkov radiation exists when this value is exceeded. The ratio of this quantity in a vacuum to this quantity in a material is that material's index of refraction. It is squared and multiplied by mass to give energy in an equation derived by Einstein, E equals m c squared. Name this theoretical upper limit for the speed of any object, equal to about three hundred million meters per second.

Calderas are formed from the collapse of these objects, which can be divided into composite, shield, and cinder cone types. The Hawaiian Islands were formed from these landforms, which are most commonly found in the Ring of Fire. Name these landforms that can be classified as active, dormant, or extinct based on the time they last erupted.

It was the subject of a Scientific American special report dealing with Modified Newtonian Dynamics by Mordechai Milgrom. This substance was first proposed in 1934 by Fritz Zwicky to make up for "missing mass" in the universe. Its non-baryonic variety contains no mass. Identify this type of matter in the universe named due to its unobservability.

This shape is traced out by the set of all points that are equidistant from a focus and a directrix. It is the only conic section that can be graphed as a function. It is the shape of the height versus time graph of a ball tossed straight in the air. Identify this shape that is traced out by the graph of any quadratic function.

The Aufbau principle explains how these particles are placed in their "shells." The discovery of these particles in cathode rays by J.J. Thomson led him to formulate the plum pudding model. The charge on one of these particles is also known as the fundamental charge. In the Bohr model of the atom, these particles orbit the nucleus. Name these negatively charged particles.

The poorwill is the only bird to demonstrate this behavior, which can be defined as sustained torpor. It is called estivation if it occurs during the summer. Animals must either collect or eat lots of food during the fall so that they do not starve while doing it. Name this behavior in which an animal goes into a deep sleep for the entire winter.

The Alinda and Griqua groups of these objects are found within the Kirkwood Gaps. The Atens, Amors, and Apollos are three groups of these objects whose orbits come near the Earth. The first of these objects was discovered at a point that filled a gap in Bode's Law. Name these objects that include Ceres and Vesta, which are most prominently found in a "belt" between Mars and Jupiter.

The D double prime layer lies in the lowest part of this region. The upper part of this region mainly consists of magnesium-iron silicates such as pyroxene and olivine. This layer extends to a depth of 2890 kilometers and contains more than half the Earth's mass. Name this molten layer of the Earth that is found between the crust and the core.

The uniform probability distribution takes this shape. Rotating this shape using one of its sides as an axis yields a cylinder. This shape is traced out by the x-axis, the y-axis, and the equations x equals two and y equals six. Each diagonal of this kind of quadrilateral divides it into two congruent right triangles. Give this shape that has four right angles.

One variant of this organelle is found in muscle cells and stores calcium. Like the Golgi body, it is composed of flattened sacks called cisternae. This set of tubes contains chaperone proteins, which help fold proteins. Those proteins are synthesized in the ribosomes, which are attached to one form of this organelle. Name this "packaging center" of the cell, which is divided into rough and smooth types.

An ideal blackbody is an object that absorbs all energy transferred by this process. This is the process in which energy is transferred from the Sun to the Earth, because it is the only form of heat exchange that can pass through a vacuum. It takes its name from the fact that it emits energy in all directions. Name this type of heat exchange that differs from convection and conduction.

Modifications of this process can use PEP carboxylase ("PEP" car-BOX-ill-ase) to fix a reactant normally fixed by RuBisCO (roo-BISS-ko) in this process's dark reactions. The light reactions of this process occur along the thylakoid ("THIGH"-luh-koyd) membrane. It takes place within the chloroplasts (KLOR-oh-plasts), which contain light-absorbing chlorophylls (KLOR-oh-fills). Name this process by which organisms, often plants, use light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose.

Starburst types of these systems have unusually high supplies of gas, and they can combine in a process known as cannibalism. The "tuning fork diagram" is a graphic depiction of the Hubble classification scheme for these systems, which divides them into irregular, elliptical and spiral types. M31 is the Andromeda one. Name these regions of the universe that include the Milky Way.

The rest type of this concept is described in special relativity. Its rotational analogue is rotational inertia. It equals energy divided by the square of the speed of light. On Earth, it is sometimes confused with weight, though it is measured not in pounds but in grams. Name this quantity that represents the amount of matter in an object.

Fatty acids contain long chains of hydrogen and this element. Methane consists of four hydrogens bonded to this element. One form of this element in a cylindrical structure is the strongest known material, and is known as a namesake nanotube. Organic chemistry is the study of molecules containing this element. Its allotropes include diamond and graphite. Name this element that makes up all living things.

Gaussian elimination can reduce these mathematical entities into row echelon form. Their addition is commutative, but generally, multiplication of them is not. The determinant can only be found in square ones; and in a two by two one, the determinant can be found using the formula ad-bc. Name this term for a set of numbers arranged in a rectangular box usually offset by brackets.

Arthur Doodson designed a machine for predicting the magnitude of these events. They occur in a cycle that includes "stand" periods followed by "slack water" periods. An unusually high concentration of dinoflagellates (DYE-no-FLADGE-ell-ates) can cause the "red" type. Weak versions of these events are known as "neap" ones and occur in the first and third quarters of the lunar cycle. Name these variations in the sea level.

Like the kidney, this organ possesses large amounts of smooth endoplasmic reticulum because of its role in removing toxins from the body. This organ converts glycogen into glucose and creates cholesterol. This largest human internal organ is divided into four lobes and can regenerate. Cirrhosis is the degeneration of, which reddish-brown abdominal organ, which produces bile and stores it in the gallbladder?

A triangular patch of clouds that circulates this planet quickly is known as The Scooter. Its atmosphere contains the fastest winds in the solar system. Its existence was predicted by Alexis Bouvard, and it was discovered by Johann Galle. It often contains the Great Dark Spot. Its largest moon, which has a retrograde orbit, is Triton. Name this gas giant, the farthest from the Sun in the solar system.

In conics, if this value is less than 0, a circle or ellipse forms. If this value is 0 in cubic functions, there is one root of multiplicity 2. If this value is positive in a quadratic equation, then there are two real solutions; and the formula for finding this value in a quadratic equation is b squared minus four a c. Name this value which can be used to determine the nature of roots of a function.

This structure is divided into Brodmann areas, and develops from the telencephalon. The corpus callosum ("CORE"-puss kuh-LOE-sum) connects the two hemispheres of this structure, which is divided into temporal, parietal, occipital, and frontal lobes. Name this largest area of the brain, which controls voluntary thoughts and actions.

The Bernoulli one approximates the powers of x plus 1 to a linear equation using the power for the slope. The "triangle" one sets a restriction for the possible lengths of the third side of a triangle given the other two. Dividing by a negative number results in a sign change in, what mathematical statement about relative size of two entities, characterized by use of greater-than and less-than signs?

This constellation contains the Trapezium Cluster and is the site of a late-October meteor shower. One of its stars, formerly known as the Amazon Star, is Bellatrix, and its brightest stars are Betelgeuse and Rigel. Its namesake nebula joins with Hatysa and other stars to form its sword, while Alnitak, Alnilam, and Mintaka form its belt. Name this constellation nicknamed the Hunter.

Both Globular Cluster M54, the center of this constellation's namesake dwarf elliptical galaxy, and a possible supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way are found in this constellation. Unusually, its brightest star is its epsilon star, Kaus Australis, found in its Milk Dipper, or Teapot, asterism. Name this constellation found between Ophiucus and Capricorn, which depicts an archer.

Hilbert's Grand Hotel paradox is a thought experiment concerning this concept in sets, and taking the limit to it is used to find a function's horizontal asymptote. Irrational numbers are defined to have this quantity of digits, and Euclid proved that there are this many prime numbers. Name this concept in math which is defined as the largest, boundless quantity.

This man found that nothing would grow in nutrient broth unless it was exposed to the air, thereby rejecting the theory of spontaneous generation and providing evidence for germ theory. He generalized Edward Jenner's work with smallpox immunity to develop vaccines for anthrax and rabies. Name this French scientist who engineered a namesake process to destroy microorganisms in milk and other food products.

An alpha particle is a nucleus of this element, which has a filled 1s (ONE S) orbital but no p orbitals at ground state. After the Hindenburg disaster, this gas replaced hydrogen in zeppelins and blimps. Because the speed of sound in this gas is much faster than that in air, inhaling it causes a high-pitched voice. Name this lightest noble gas, with atomic number two and symbol He (H-E).

This force allows accelerated rolling motion down an incline by producing a net torque on the object. In general, this nonconservative force is equal to the normal force times mu, its namesake coefficient, and it converts kinetic energy into internal energy. For a given object, the kinetic variety is less than the static type. Name this force between surfaces that opposes the motion of an object.

The fundamental units in these body parts work according to the sliding-filament hypothesis and are called sarcomeres. The type that surrounds hollow organs such as the stomach is the smooth type, and the other two types are cardiac and skeletal. One of them, the diaphragm, ultimately fails in a namesake kind of "dystrophy." name these human organs necessary for movement, which include triceps and biceps.

Ribosome subunits pass through pores in this structure's namesake envelope and are produced in one part of it. In one kind of cloning, this organelle is transferred into an egg that lacks one. The presence of this organelle distinguishes eukaryotes from prokaryotes. This organelle divides in two during mitosis because DNA is found here. Name this information processing area of the cell.

The name for the physical state of the universe during this event was explained and named by Stephen Hawking. Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation is left over from just after this event, which was hypothesized by Georges Lemaître. Hubble's use of the Doppler Effect helped to prove that this event occurred. Name this event in cosmological history during which the universe started to expand rapidly.

When this substance is used, it often leaves behind a liquid with naphthalene and various phenols. The lowest rank of this type of substance, formed from peat, is lignite, while higher grades are classified as anthracite or the bituminous type. Plant remains over a long period of time transform into this sedimentary rock. Name this substance which is used to generate electricity after it is mined out of the ground.

A hyperbolic form of this function is defined for a variable x as one-half times quantity e to the x plus e to the minus x. The law of this function states that, for a triangle ABC, c squared equals a squared plus b squared minus 2 a b times this function of the angle C. One over this function of x is the secant of x. Name this function equal to the length of the adjacent side over that of the hypotenuse.

Metallic bonds can be modeled as "seas" of these particles. In another model, the repulsion between pairs of them leads to molecular shapes like trigonal planar and octahedral. The fundamental charge is the charge of one of these particles, which can be found in s, p, d, and f orbitals. J.J. Thomson discovered, which negatively-charged components of the atom that orbit the nucleus?

The first step in this process can be further broken down into leptotene, zygotene, and pachytene phases. A common problem during this process is nondisjunction, which leads to conditions such as Klinefelter's Syndrome and Down Syndrome. This process involves two instances of prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase. Name this process used to create haploid cells, such as sperm and eggs.

This constellation's alpha star is the brightest in the Hyades ("HIGH"-uh-deez) cluster. One object in this constellation is the remnant of a supernova observed in 1054 AD. In addition to the Crab Nebula, this constellation also contains the Pleiades (PLEE-uh-deez). Its beta star, Al Nath, is found next to Auriga, while its alpha star is Aldebaran (all-DEB-uh-ron). Name this constellation that depicts a bull.

Two brothers of this surname discovered piezoelectricity and a namesake point at which ferromagnetic materials become paramagnetic. One of those brothers explored the properties of the ore pitchblende with his wife. That wife later won a second Nobel Prize for her work isolating radium, and named the element polonium after her native country. Give the last name of physicist Pierre and his wife Marie.

This shape names a law for adding vectors. In a namesake illusion, diagonals of two of these figures appear to be different lengths, though they are not. Though not necessarily the same length, the diagonals of this quadrilateral bisect each other. If all four sides of this type of figure are of equal length, the figure is a rhombus. Name this shape drawn from two intersecting sets of parallel lines.

These objects contain columns called seracs and tubes called moulins. They create kame (CAME) and kettle topography as well as drumlins, which are land forms in the shape of whales, and kettles, which are generally shallow lakes. The debris they leave behind is often called a moraine. Name these large long-lasting accumulations of snow and ice, found in places such as a namesake Montana national park.

Cushion plants are found in the alpine form of this biome, which is also home to marmots, pikas, and chinchillas. The point at which this biome meets taiga is known as the treeline. Flora in this biome consists of lichens (LYE-kens) and mosses. Non-alpine forms of it have little vegetation due to permafrost. Name this biome that lacks tree growth, which can be found in Alaska and is home to caribou and reindeer.

This body contains an unusually reflective equatorial region known as Xanadu. It is in a 3:4 orbital resonance with Hyperion. In 2010, the Cassini-Huygens probe found evidence of a cryovolcano named Sotra Facula on this moon. This moon's surface contains methane lakes, and it has a dense, opaque atmosphere. Name this largest moon of Saturn.

The energy of electromagnetic waves is obtained by multiplying Planck's constant "h" by this quantity. When an object such as a bridge vibrates at the natural state of this quantity, resonance occurs. For rotating devices, it is symbolized by omega and expressed in revolutions per second. Name this property referring to the number of occurrences of a repeating event per unit time, which is measured in Hertz.

This process's namesake constant is used in Fick's Law and an explanation of Brownian motion. This process is used during respiration to get oxygen into blood, and it then replaces that oxygen with carbon dioxide. It is synonymous with heat conduction, and this process in water is called osmosis. Name this process in which the random motion of particles causes them to spread to areas of lower concentration.

Apollonius' Theorem can be used to find the length of this construct given the side lengths of a triangle. Three of them divide a triangle into six triangles with equal areas, and they intersect at the centroid, or center of mass. Identify this term that in geometry refers to a line drawn from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side and in statistics refers to the middle number in a list.

In one common lab demo, a balloon is shattered after being treated with nitrogen in this form. At room temperature and standard pressure, only bromine and mercury are in this phase. These substances are used to fill a tube in thermometers and barometers. They take the shape of their container, but do not expand to fill it, unlike gases. Name this state of matter that can boil and is produced by melting.

All solutions of Diophantine (DYE-oh-FAN-teen) equations are in this set. This set is closed under addition, subtraction, and multiplication, but not division, and is denoted by a boldface Z. The absolute value of any number in this set except 0 is a natural number. Rational numbers can be expressed as the quotient of two of these kinds of numbers. Give the term that applies to the set of whole numbers and their negatives.

In rotational motion, this quantity can be obtained by taking one half of the moment of inertia times the angular velocity squared. In an elastic collision, both momentum and this quantity are conserved. It equals one half times mass times velocity squared. Name this energy of objects in motion, contrasted with the potential type.

Genes related to this condition include the c-sis and p53 genes. The human papillomavirus (pahp-uh- LOH-muh-veye-ruhs), HPV, can cause one form of this disease, which is known as a sarcoma when it affects connective tissue and a melanoma if affects the skin. Metastasis (muh-TAS-tuh-sis) refers to the spread of this disease to other organs. It is caused by malignant tumors. Name this uncontrolled growth of cells often treated with chemotherapy.

Several "pancake domes" mark the surface of this body, whose other features include the Gula Mons and Sif Mons mountains. The spacecraft Vega 1 and 2 landed on this body. Due to a runaway greenhouse effect, the average surface temperature on this body is over seven hundred degrees Kelvin. Name this home of Ishtar Terra, the most similar planet to Earth.

A group of genes coding for lactose breakdown, known as the lac operon, was first discovered in this model organism. Although it is not Shigella, shiga toxins are produced in virulent strains of this organism such as its serotype O157:H7. They colonize the human gut at birth. Name these gramnegative bacteria that are a common cause of food poisoning and food recalls.

This term originated from shapes that had non-integer dimensions. One of them is composed of repeating cardioids and circles. Other examples include the Sierpinski Triangle, which consists of repeating equilateral triangles within a larger triangle, and the Koch snowflake, which has an infinite perimeter but a finite area. Name these self-similar mathematical constructs that include the Mandelbrot one.

Lewis defined these substances as acceptors of electron pairs. The presence of the hydronium ion is necessary in the Arrhenius definition. Strong examples of these substances include nitric and sulfuric, which fit the Bronsted-Lowry model as donors of hydrogen ions and turn blue litmus paper red. Name these substances with pH lower than 7 that neutralize bases.

A "pillow" form of this substance forms underwater. "Domes" of this substance form from andesite. This substance can be classified, depending on the smoothness of its surface, as a'a (AH-AH) or pahoehoe (pah-HOY-HOY). It accumulates around a vent to form a cinder cone, and it solidifies to form igneous rock. Give the term for magma that reaches the Earth's surface, often through a volcanic explosion.

This is the only element for which Schrodinger's equation can be solved exactly. Isotopes of this element include tritium and deuterium. Its diatomic form is released when sodium reacts with water. It is the only nonmetal in Period 1 of the periodic table. Name this lightest element, which has a chemical symbol of H.

A system's Lagrangian (lah-GRAN-jee-uhn) equals this quantity minus potential energy. This quantity can be found by dividing the square of an objects momentum by twice its mass. The change in this quantity for an object is equal to the net work done on the object. It equals one-half times mass times velocity squared. Name this type of energy that objects possess because of motion.

These entities can be found by using the Sieve of Eratosthenes (AIR-uh-TOSS-the-neez). According to Goldbach's conjecture, every integer greater than two can be expressed as a sum of two of them. Every positive integer can be expressed as a factorization of these numbers. Identify these natural numbers whose only divisors are themselves and one.

The antibiotic erythromycin works by disrupting this organelle, which contains E, P, and A sites on its large subunit. The parts of this organelle are assembled at nucleoli (noo-klee-OH-lye), and when bound to a membrane, these create the rough ER. Codons are translated at this organelle where the tRNA and mRNA meet. Name this organelle that is the site of protein synthesis

These objects explained the Vine-Matthews hypothesis about the reversal of the Earth's magnetic field. Seafloor spreading occurs at divergent boundaries between these objects.
